clue.text: Change in nude composition is no different

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
one word is placed inside the other, sitting in the middle of it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to change something is to alter it

explanation.surface: An artist reworks a nude painting, yet the picture ends up looking just the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the word that goes inside; 'composition' is what rearranges the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaltered has not been changed, so it is no different from before; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Relative part of overrun cleared

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, so the answer lies inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A relative clears up after something has overrun, perhaps a flooded kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, a parent's brother, so he is a relative.

clue.text: Forgetting disease, Continent accepts lost men

indicators.note: men who are lost have wandered off course, so their letters are jumbled
to accept is to take in, so the continent holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: Asia is a continent
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A news story: an illness causing memory loss, as a continent takes in men who have gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is a medical condition in which memory is lost, a disorder of forgetting.

clue.text: Forty heading off mutinous novice

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off means it is removed
mutinous letters rebel against their order and so get rearranged

blocks.note: the number written as a word

explanation.surface: Forty sailors set off on a mutiny led by an inexperienced beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first letter of FORTY leaves ORTY, which is rearranged as TYRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or learner, someone new to an activity, just as a novice is.

clue.text: She is badly hurt

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the following letters come out disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A short report that a woman has been seriously injured.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth is a female name, so it can stand for She; the word ruth is also an old word for pity, apt for someone hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a woman's name, as of the biblical heroine, so a pronoun for a woman can stand in for it.

clue.text: Intended to ponder

blocks.note: first meaning: an adjective, done on purpose
second meaning: a verb, to think something over carefully

explanation.walkthrough: The word is said differently in each sense: the adjective ends with -rit, the verb with -rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate act is one done on purpose, and to deliberate is to consider at length before deciding.

clue.text: Elegant son's craving

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a craving is a strong wish

explanation.surface: A boy longs for something smart and stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British slang for smart and fashionable, so it means elegant.

clue.text: Party World: a lighthouse in Aberdeen originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, the letter it begins with

blocks.note: Saturn is a planet, a world
taken as written
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An event listing: a party at a lighthouse in the Scottish city of Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturnalia was a Roman winter festival, and the word now means any wild party or revel.

clue.text: Separate unit's very unpunctual

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit
so means very, as in so good
someone unpunctual arrives late

explanation.surface: A complaint that a separate army unit keeps turning up behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart from others, a verb synonym of separate.

clue.text: Hated holding knotted ties, so hung back

indicators.note: knotted things are twisted and tangled, so these letters are mixed up
to hold something is to keep it within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who loathed wearing tied neckties dawdled before getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged ties go in after the first letter only, not around the whole word; 'so' is just a joining word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause or hold back from acting, so hung back is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Congo naturalist's broadcast: well done!

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A wildlife presenter in the Congo is praised for a fine television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means has: the naturalist has broadcast. Only the two words before it are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying well done is offering praise for an achievement, which is what congratulations express.

clue.text: In space asteroid's veering towards orient

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning a word break

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the first three of the second

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: a rock in space is changing course and swinging round towards the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the old name for the countries of Asia, the East, so orient and east are synonyms.

clue.text: Sailor's wayward, markedly different from the norm

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor; the 's means is
errant means straying from the proper course

explanation.surface: A sailor behaves badly, quite unlike the usual crew member.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant describes something that departs from what is normal or expected, a straight dictionary match.

clue.text: Impromptu action with the wrist?

blocks.note: the plain meaning: done without preparation
read literally, a movement made away from the shirt sleeve's end at the wrist

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the idiom for speaking unprepared comes from notes jotted on a shirt cuff, and the wrist is where a cuff sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without preparation is speaking spontaneously, which the idiom about a shirt cuff describes.

clue.text: Water-based paint, no coloured emulsion initially, in moderation

indicators.note: initially asks for the starting letter of each of the words it follows

blocks.note: tempera is a paint made with egg yolk and water
N is a standard abbreviation for no
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: use water-based paint and no tinted emulsion, all done in moderation.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance is self-restraint, avoiding excess, especially with alcohol, so it means moderation.

clue.text: Show fur, reportedly, to driver

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: said quickly the two words sound like the job title

explanation.surface: Someone displays a fur coat to the person who drives them about.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a person employed to drive a car for someone else, so a driver.

clue.text: Arrives carrying support and replies

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: arrives means comes
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone turns up bringing support and answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Comebacks are quick retorts, so they are replies, usually witty ones.

clue.text: Expert in part of the store

blocks.note: a department, abbreviated dept, is a section of a large shop

explanation.surface: A specialist works in one section of a department store.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a skilled person, a master of some art, so an expert.

clue.text: Intended as average time

blocks.note: the mean is a kind of average
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something was meant to take an average amount of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past tense of mean, to intend, so meant is a synonym of intended.

clue.text: Country's changed regalia

indicators.note: the following word has been altered, so its letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation has replaced its royal or state ceremonial insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a country of North Africa, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Scared when favourite one's fired, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the words are only a possible version, so their letters can be rearranged

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee is terrified on hearing that the boss's favourite has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: PET is followed by the letters of I and FIRED rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified literally means turned to stone, and figuratively frozen with fear, so scared.

clue.text: Motivation shown as time's up, anyway

indicators.note: any way means in any order at all, so the letters may be arranged freely

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A deadline arriving is what gets people moving, at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or drive that makes something happen, so a motivation.

clue.text: Insect animals find to be fearful pests

blocks.note: a bug is an insect
bears are animals, an example

explanation.surface: Someone finds insects and animals alike to be frightening nuisances.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of annoyance or dread, originally an imaginary bogey, so a feared pest.

clue.text: Great drama when recipe's returned without touching

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters for the following word are taken out
something returned goes back the way it came, so the word reads from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning, touching on

explanation.surface: A cookery mishap: a recipe sent back untouched turns into high drama.
explanation.walkthrough: RECIPE loses its opening RE to leave CIPE, which then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic poem or grand film, a work of great drama on a large scale.

clue.text: About poem's rules

blocks.note: C, for circa, means about
an ode is a poem, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A query concerning the conventions of a poem's form.
explanation.definitionFit: Codes are systems of laws or regulations, such as a dress code, so rules.

clue.text: First lady's kind of pudding

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to Eve, the first woman in Genesis
second meaning: ... pudding, a British baked dessert of apples under sponge

explanation.walkthrough: First lady suggests a president's wife, but here she is Eve of the Bible. Eve's pudding is a British baked apple sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve was the first woman in the Bible, and the apple sponge dessert is named after her.

clue.text: Plain fruit, reportedly

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: the ugli is a wrinkled Jamaican citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone claims a fruit is said to be unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain describes someone not good-looking, a gentler word for unattractive.

clue.text: Went around with iced rum, vacating ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the words before it are pulverised into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A sailor drinks iced rum and leaves the land behind on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To circumnavigate is to sail or travel all the way round something, such as the globe.

clue.text: Employees' greasy food sent back to France

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: fats make food greasy
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Workers' oily canteen meals are shipped back to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff are the people employed by an organisation, collectively its workforce.

clue.text: Latter day, sassiest assembly of writers

indicators.note: the latter part of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
an assembly puts parts together, so the letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting of the cheekiest modern authors, gathered in the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Essayists are writers who specialise in essays, short prose pieces, so they are a kind of writer.
